questionText: What is the difference between JSON serialization and deserialization?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can distinguish JSON serialization from deserialization, relate each direction to an API boundary, and explain why request and response shapes need not match.
inScope: Non-lossless round trips and sensitive-field boundaries
Separate contract tests for each direction

claims.statement: JSON serialization writes a Java value into a JSON representation, while deserialization reads JSON into a declared Java target type.
Successful JSON-to-Java mapping establishes that conversion succeeded, but Bean Validation constraints and service-level domain rules remain separate checks.
An API can deliberately accept one JSON shape and return another because client input, server-generated data, and public output have different responsibilities.

examples.title: Compile and run the exact example with different request and response records

validation.command: Run mvn -q test with Java 17 and the Spring Boot 3.3.1 managed Jackson version against the exact JsonDirectionExample
validation.expected: The request JSON is read into CreateOrderRequest; the response JSON contains id, productId, and status but does not contain request-only quantity

review.notes: Spring message-conversion behavior and Jakarta Validation boundaries were checked against official documentation. The revised Java 17 example passed with the Jackson version managed by Spring Boot 3.3.1 and proved the distinct response shape.
